**No, the first wave can't start.** The preflight record would fail the check in at least five ways, and the plan isn't set up for an unattended run. One of the failures only a person can fix: the repository token has already expired.

I couldn't run `check_orchestration.py` because this session has no shell tool. So the preflight verdict below is `Not run`, and every failure listed is my own reading of the two files against `references/autonomy-preflight.md`, not checker output.

**What I found:** Hold the first wave (the record would come back `FAIL`). The deciding fact: `A1` `REPO_TOKEN` expired at `2026-11-14T03:00Z`, and it's now 2026-11-16, so no agent could reach the repository or CI tonight.

**Why it matters:** An unattended plan can't pass its final gate without a preflight record that still passes (`PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED`). Starting now would either lose ten hours of work at the merge boundary or stop the run at its first push. Fixing these before 22:00 costs one evening of setup.

**Do this first:**
1. Issue a non-interactive `REPO_TOKEN` that's valid past tomorrow 08:00 and re-run probe `E1` at `3f9c2e1`. Only a person can do this.
2. Fix the plan and the account conflict (see table), then write a new preflight record bound to the plan's digest.
3. Run `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py preflight .alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .` and start only on `PASS`.

**What I did not check:**
- The checker verdict for the plan or the preflight record (run the command in step 3, and `... plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .`).
- Whether the "approve the plan" step has actually happened. Your confirmation closes it.
- Whether the work tree is clean at `3f9c2e1` (`git status`, `git rev-parse HEAD`).
- Whether the host stays awake for the whole window.

| # | Problem | Where | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | The repo token expired 2026-11-14 03:00Z, before even the recorded window ended | `preflight.json:62` | `CREDENTIAL_EXPIRES` |
| 2 | The window recorded is 2026-11-13 22:00Z to 11-14 08:00Z, which is three nights ago and not tonight. "22:00 tonight" also needs your time zone, because the record uses Z (UTC). | `preflight.json:4-5` | Window re-check (§3) |
| 3 | The record has no `plan` field (digest and base), so it isn't tied to this plan's revision | `preflight.json` | `SCHEMA` / `PREFLIGHT_STALE` |
| 4 | The plan lacks `execution.unattended: true`, and no package has `needs`. P1 and P2 run commands (`npm test -- …`) without declaring what they need to run them. The earlier "passed" plan check didn't apply the unattended rules. | `plan.json:15-22`, packages | `NEEDS_UNDECLARED` |
| 5 | No preflight entry has `covers`, so once needs are declared, none of them is claimed | `access`, `accounts`, `environment` | `PREREQUISITE_UNCOVERED` |
| 6 | Account `U1` (clerk-a, can write data) is used by both P1 and P2, which run at the same time in wave 1. It isn't read-only, so they can't share it. | `preflight.json:84-87` | `ACCOUNT_CONFLICT` |
| 7 | Probe `E4` signs in as `clerk-b auditor`, but the record has no clerk-b account. A clerk-b account (`U2`) for P2 looks like it was dropped, and it would fix #6. | `preflight.json:151` | Judgment (wrong thing probed) |

These parts hold up: the work entries (I1 is READY, I2 is PARTLY-READY and reversible), both decisions are made by a human (D2 is a reversible default you confirm at merge), the baseline `npm test` (`E6`) passed at the base, the escalation channel was tested (`E7`), human steps fall only before or at the end, no secret values appear in the record, the concurrency cap is 2 with P1 and P2 writing to separate folders, and P3 reviews without having written either package.
